The Joy of Giving

A Most of us believe that more money would make us happier. But some of the richest people in the world have decided that the best thing to do with a fortune is to give it away.

B Chuck Feeney was one of them. In 1960 he started Duty Free Shoppers, the airport shops, with a business partner and became a billionaire. For many years, almost nobody knew that he was giving his money away in secret, through a foundation called The Atlantic Philanthropies. In total he gave about eight billion dollars to universities, hospitals and other good causes. He himself lived in a small rented flat, flew economy class and wore a cheap watch. His foundation closed in 2020, when there was no money left to give, and he died in 2023, aged 92.

C Feeney's example inspired two other billionaires, Bill Gates and Warren Buffett. In 2010 they started the Giving Pledge — a promise to give away more than half of your fortune. More than 200 of the world's richest people have already signed it.

D But you don't have to be rich to be generous. From 2009 to 2024, a British charity, the Charities Aid Foundation, asked people in more than 100 countries three questions every year: in the past month, have you helped a stranger? Have you given money to a charity? Have you done any volunteer work? Their World Giving Index put countries in order, and some of the most generous were not rich at all. Indonesia came first seven years in a row.

E Uzbekistan has its own tradition of giving time: hashar. When a family needs to build a house, or a street needs to be cleaned, neighbours come and work together for free — and afterwards, everyone shares a meal.

F So perhaps the question is not how much we have, but what we do with it. Have you given anything away yet this month?

2

Grammar · present perfect with already and yet

TUSHUNTIRISH — ALREADY VA YET

A already = allaqachon boʻldi — koʻpincha kutilganidan ertaroq. have / has bilan uchinchi shakl orasiga qoʻyiladi: I've already given £50. · More than 200 people have already signed the Pledge.

B yet = hozirgacha. Inkor va soʻroq gaplarda, gap oxirida: We haven't sold the books yet. · Have you paid yet? Qisqa javob: Not yet.

C Tugagan vaqt yoʻq. yesterday, last week, in 2020 bilan Past Simple: I've already paid. → I paid yesterday. — I've already paid yesterday emas.

D Istisnolar. Savoldagi already ajablanishni bildiradi: Have you already spent all your money?! yet hech qachon tasdiq gapda ishlatilmaydi: I've finished yet emas → I've already finished. Notoʻgʻri feʼllarning uchinchi shaklini yodlang: give → given · do → done · make → made · pay → paid · spend → spent · sell → sold · buy → bought.

DIQQAT — KOʻP UCHRAYDIGAN XATOLAR

1 ✗ I already have given it away. → ✓ I've already given it away. — already have dan keyin.

2 ✗ I haven't already paid. → ✓ I haven't paid yet. — inkorda yet.

3 ✗ Did you send the money yet? → ✓ Have you sent the money yet? — Present Perfect.

4 ✗ We've already raised it last week. → ✓ We raised it last week. — tugagan vaqt = Past Simple.

5 ✗ She has give all her old clothes away. → ✓ She has given … — uchinchi shakl.

3.1 Read Sardor's post. Look at the phrases in bold.

MY YEAR AS A VOLUNTEER

Last year I did some volunteer work at a children's hospital in Samarkand. I didn't earn any money, but I made a lot of friends there. On Saturdays we did something fun with the children — drawing, games, music. My uncle gave me some good advice: “Make a note of everything the nurses tell you.” On my first day I got lost, and a doctor gave me directions to the playroom. I tried hard to do a good job, even when I was tired. Now I give some money away every month: I make a small payment online to the hospital. It isn't much, but it really makes me happy.

5

Writing · an update email

TUSHUNTIRISH — XATBOSHILAR

A Bitta xatboshi — bitta fikr. Yangi fikrni boshlaganda yangi xatboshi boshlang va xatboshilar orasida bitta qator tashlang. Birinchi gap xatboshi nima haqida ekanini aytadi.

B Yangilik xati toʻrt qismdan iborat: 1 nega yozyapsiz (rahmat + asosiy yangilik) · 2 nima boʻldi · 3 pul nimaga sarflanadi · 4 keyingi tadbir + yana rahmat.

C Foydali iboralar: This email is to say a big thank you to … · I'm writing to let you know … · We've (already) raised … · The money will help … · Our next event is … · Thanks again for all your help.

MODEL — AN UPDATE EMAIL

Subject: We've raised 7,450,000 so'm — thank you!

Dear friends,

1 This email is to say a big thank you to everyone who came to our book and cake sale on Saturday. We've raised 7,450,000 so'm for the children's hospital — much more than we expected!

2 Many of you baked cakes, and some of you brought old books from home. Students from Group 214 sold drinks, and our teachers did a great job at the cash desk. We've already sold almost all the books, but we haven't sold the dictionaries yet — so if you need one, please ask!

3 The hospital will use the money to buy toys and books for its playroom. Many children stay there for weeks, so a bright playroom really makes them happy.

4 Our next event is a sponsored walk in May. Would you like to join us? Thanks again for all your help.

Best wishes, Malika (Student Council)
